Context/Background: Renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features (sRCC) is a highly aggressive tumor type yet preferentially responds to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). sRCC is unique in its ability to develop from various epithelial RCC subtypes, most frequently ccRCC, and sarcomatoid features typically exist as foci nested within an epithelioid RCC. Sarcomatoid clones are thought to arise from transformation of an epithelioid RCC cell through epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).To better understand microenvironmental mediators of the paradoxical immune sensitivity of sRCC, we performed single-cell analyses of human sRCC tumors compared against clear cell RCC (ccRCC), with validation spatially and in bulk transcriptomic datasets totaling over 3,000 RCC tumors.
Prompt: Gene expression counts were aggregated by case and differential expression analysis on pseudobulked counts was performed. Based on the differential gene expression results, run GSEA on hallmark genesets, and provide a brief discussion of pathways important in the sRCC vs ccRCC context. From the top 20 differentially expressed genes, prioritize 5 genes and discuss their possible roles in tumorigenesis and sarcomatoid transformation.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Single‐cell pseudobulk differential expression (sRCC vs. ccRCC) was performed on aggregated case‐level counts from Salgia et al. (2025). 14,871 genes were tested; the top of the ranked list showed strong upregulation of EMT‐ and ECM‐associated genes in the sarcomatoid component. Replicate numbers, tumor grade/stage, and normalization details are not specified.  

Keywords  
• EMT  
• Immune response  
• Extracellular matrix  
• Cell adhesion  
• TGF-β signaling  

Candidate Genes  
CD44, SEMA3C, DCBLD2, TEAD2, PLAU  

Pathway Enrichments  
Library: MSigDB_Hallmark_2020  
Up: 9 pathways (90%), Down: 1 pathway (10%), up/down ratio = 9.0  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP)  
| Theme                         | Direction | Leading Genes (first 10)                                           |
|-------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition | UP        | MGP, COMP, IGFBP2, COL12A1, BGN, DKK1, TIMP1, THBS2, CD44, NTM       |
| Myogenesis                    | UP        | BDKRB2, TNNT1, PVALB, NOS1, SOD3, FGF2, MYLK, EFS, ITGB4, COL6A3    |
| KRAS Signaling Dn             | UP        | NOS1, PCDHB1, THRB, TEX15, IGFBP2, RGS11, SHOX2, PTGFR, KRT13, KCND1 |
| Coagulation                   | UP        | PLAT, CAPN2, PLG, SH2B2, CFH, DUSP6, CTSV, COMP, CAPN5, FGA        |

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN)  
| Theme                            | Direction | Leading Genes (first 10)                                     |
|----------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| TNF-alpha Signaling via NF-κB     | DOWN      | KLF2, NFKBIA, TNIP2, FOSB, IER2, TRAF1, PFKFB3, IFNGR2, NFKB1, KYNU |

Analysis  
EMT is the most highly enriched upregulated program (NES 5.25), reflecting sarcomatoid transformation with coordinated ECM remodeling (e.g., COL12A1, COMP) and adhesion/motility factors (CD44, TIMP1). Myogenesis and coagulation signatures further underscore cytoskeletal reprogramming and proteolytic microenvironment shifts. Conversely, TNFα/NF-κB signaling is selectively downregulated, suggesting loss of canonical inflammatory feedback despite overall immune sensitivity. Together, these patterns reveal a switch from epithelial/inflammatory programs toward mesenchymal/invasive states in sRCC.  

Targeted Subset (EMT-guided)  
| Data Base             | Pathway                         | NES   | Leading Genes (first 5)    |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------|-------|-----------------------------|
| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020  | Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition | 5.251 | MGP, COMP, IGFBP2, COL12A1, BGN |

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
Up-regulated (EMT)  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                                            | Pathway(s)                  |
|---------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| CD44    | UP        | HA‐receptor; cell adhesion/migration; EMT marker         | EMT, Coagulation            |
| SEMA3C  | UP        | Semaphorin; regulates ECM, angiogenesis, motility        | EMT                         |
| DCBLD2  | UP        | Endothelial receptor; vascular remodeling, invasion      | EMT                         |
| TEAD2   | UP        | Hippo‐pathway transcription factor; promotes EMT genes   | EMT                         |
| PLAU    | UP        | Urokinase plasminogen activator; ECM degradation, invasion | EMT, Coagulation           |

Down-regulated (Inflammation)  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                                         | Pathway(s)                  |
|---------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| NFKBIA  | DOWN      | IκBα; inhibits NF-κB inflammatory signaling           | TNF-α via NF-κB             |
| MYC     | DOWN      | Proto-oncogenic transcription factor; cell cycle      | TNF-α via NF-κB             |
| ICAM1   | DOWN      | Adhesion molecule; leukocyte–endothelial interaction  | TNF-α via NF-κB             |
| CCL4    | DOWN      | Chemokine; T-cell recruitment                         | TNF-α via NF-κB             |
| IL6     | DOWN      | Cytokine; B-cell maturation, acute-phase response     | TNF-α via NF-κB             |

Implications  
sRCC engages a robust EMT/ECM program that likely drives invasiveness and fibrotic niches while dampening classical NF-κB–mediated inflammation. This dichotomy may underlie the paradoxical immunotherapy sensitivity of sRCC: invasive mesenchymal tumor cells generating neo-antigens and altered stroma but retaining immune‐accessible cytokine/chemokine networks.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Perform TGF-β pathway inhibition or TEAD2 knockdown in sRCC models to test reversal of EMT signatures.  
2. Spatially map CD44 and PLAU expression relative to immune cell infiltrates in matched sRCC blocks.  
3. Assess baseline NF-κB activity (e.g., IκBα phosphorylation) in sRCC vs. ccRCC to link signaling dampening with immune phenotypes.  
4. Correlate prioritized gene expression (SEMA3C, DCBLD2) with ICB response in independent bulk cohorts to validate therapy biomarkers.
